games.name: Haggle
games.description: A two-player market duel where every price only ever falls — sell before your rival does.

games.name: Sparklight
games.description: A co-operative card game where you can see every hand but your own.

games.name: Kiln
games.description: Take every tile of one kind from a rack — and whatever you leave behind is what everyone else gets.

games.name: Brood
games.description: There is no board — only the cluster you and your rival build, until one Matriarch has all six sides closed.

games.name: Bracken
games.description: Race across the common while you close the ways through it — but you may never seal one off entirely.

games.name: Shunt
games.description: Make up the train in the fewest moves — a yard puzzle where the loco only works one end, so the order of a rake never reverses.

games.name: Clatter
games.description: Take one die from the roll and every smaller die goes to everybody else — a roll-and-write about generosity you cannot avoid.

games.name: Tacit
games.description: A co-operative trick-taker: win the right card for the right crewmate, and you are almost never allowed to say which.

games.name: Tithe
games.description: A 5×5 duel where the only moves that exist are the two tolls in your hand — and the one you spend is handed straight to your opponent.

games.name: Skyhold
games.description: Move one builder, raise one block — first to stand three storeys high wins the sky.

games.name: Cairn
games.description: A chain-clearing solitaire: a cairn is a pyramid of runed stones (a full A–K ladder). Take any exposed stone one rune above or below your hand — aces wrap to kings — and it becomes your new hand, uncovering the stones beneath. Long unbroken chains build a heat multiplier; when stuck, draw from the scree, which resets your heat and spends one of a limited number of draws. Every cairn is guaranteed to have a full-clear solution, so you are never dealt an impossible board. Clear one cairn at your pace, bank a stream of small cairns against a clock, or survive a big cairn on a hard draw budget. Solo, a daily cairn, or a peer-to-peer race on the same deal.

games.name: Skein
games.description: Drag the glowing beads until no threads cross. A crossed thread glows coral with an X where it cuts; a clean one glows cyan — move the beads until nothing crosses and the web settles green. Every web is guaranteed to have a tangle-free solution, so you are never stuck. Untangle one calm web, race a stream of small webs against a clock, or crack one big tangle on a limited number of moves. Solo, a daily web, or a peer-to-peer race on the same web.

games.name: Warble
games.description: Your voice is the controller — hum low to fly low, whistle or sing high to fly high, and keep the glowing mote on a ribbon of light to score. No mic? Slide a finger up and down to fly instead, the same game. Track a forgiving ribbon, hold a staircase of notes, or thread a narrow gauntlet where one missed gap ends the run. Solo, a daily ribbon, or a peer-to-peer race on the same course.

games.name: Hatch
games.description: A picross puzzle: the numbers count the filled squares in each row and column, and reading them reveals a hidden picture. Filling a square that's really empty is a mistake, so it rewards deduction over guessing. Play a calm 10×10, a 90-second stream of small pictures, or a three-strikes 8×8 — solo, a daily board, or a peer-to-peer race on the same board.

games.name: Glint
games.description: Two cards always share exactly one symbol — never none, never two. Spot it, tap it, and a fresh card deals the instant you do. Clear the deck, race a 90-second clock, or push a one-life streak. Play solo, chase the daily deck, or race friends peer-to-peer on the very same deck.

games.name: Brim
games.description: Hold the phone dead still while an orb of light swells — the fuller it gets, the more it's worth. Release before it overflows, and don't let a jolt make you flinch and spill it. No motion sensor? Just hold your nerve. Three modes, a daily, and a peer-to-peer race on the very same orbs.

games.name: Facet
games.description: Roll a die around a grid so the right number lands face-up on each rune, then reach the vault in as few rolls as you can. Opposite faces add up to 7, so the short path is rarely the smart one. Three modes, a daily board, and a peer-to-peer race on the very same board.

games.name: Waft
games.description: Wave your hand in front of the camera to catch drifting fireflies before they fade — clean catches build a combo, wasps break it. No camera? Just tap. Solo, a daily swarm, or race a friend on the very same fireflies peer-to-peer.

games.name: Wordloom
games.description: Letters arrive one at a time — drop each into a grid, and when it's full every row and column scores its best word. You can't move a letter once it's down, so each square is a bet on two words at once. Solo, a daily grid, or race a friend on the same letters peer-to-peer.

games.name: Squirm
games.description: Slide a critter face-down, name it — the truth, or a lie. Your rival must believe you, call your bluff, or peek and pass it on with a lie of their own. Collect four of a kind and you're out. Solo vs bots, or peer-to-peer with friends.

games.name: Teeter
games.description: Tilt your phone to roll a marble through a maze to the exit — dodge the pits, grab the gems, beat the clock. Fastest time wins. No sensor? Drag or use the arrow keys. Solo, a daily, or race a friend on the same maze.

games.name: Outsize
games.description: Which country is bigger? Tap the one with more people, more land, or more crowding — build a streak as the gap between them tightens every round. Solo, a daily, or race a friend.

games.name: Landbridge
games.description: Hop country to country along shared land borders — from here to there in the fewest steps. The game knows the shortest route; can you beat it? Solo, a daily, or racing friends.

games.name: Beeline
games.description: Home in on a hidden country. Each guess tells you how far it is, which way it lies and how warm you're getting — solve it in as few as you can, on a shared daily or racing friends.

games.name: Amble
games.description: An unhurried journey down one road — but the traveller furthest behind always goes next, so every stop you race to is a turn you hand your rivals. Solo or 2–5 over a link.

games.name: Kilter
games.description: Stack bricks that really fall — no grid, real physics, so the tower leans and teeters and you lose by toppling. Race a friend to the height line, or balance a spire on a plinth barely a brick wide.

games.name: Uproar
games.description: Pass the phone and get louder than the last person — the mic keeps score, the bar keeps climbing, and your nerve runs out first.

games.name: Ballast
games.description: Stack the falling pieces and clear rows — but the well hangs from a pivot, so pile up on one side and it lists, pieces slide downhill, and the far side goes out of reach.

games.name: Unstrung
games.description: Cut words out of one long strand of letters — every cut splices in fresh thread, and a word that spans the seam scores triple.

games.name: Undercut
games.description: Race strategy with no driving — call the pit windows, read the weather, and beat the field on a decision.

games.name: Boxbox
games.description: Call the pit stop — read the telemetry and the driver's radio, fix what's broken, skip what isn't, and beat the clock.

games.name: Rootbound
games.description: A boardless hex duel: grow one shared colony that must never split, and ring your rival's Heartroot before they ring yours.

games.name: Sporeline
games.description: Maze tower-defence where your towers are the walls — fold the road longer to kill more, then send spores into a rival's field.

games.name: Lastlight
games.description: One generator holds back the cold — every building only works inside its shrinking ring of warmth.

games.name: Turntide
games.description: Draughts where a jump never kills — leap an enemy and it flips to your colour, so all 24 stones stay on the board.

games.name: Changeling
games.description: Real chess with one rule bolted on: capture a piece and yours turns into it, so your queen taking a pawn becomes a pawn.

games.name: Frostward
games.description: A cone of frost sweeps the board like a searchlight — bend the wind away from your hearths and it points at someone else.

games.name: Deepwatch
games.description: A silent co-op dive: surface a hand of deep-sea creatures in order with no numbers and no talking — all you know is who hasn't played yet.

games.name: Emberwake
games.description: Outrun a rising wall of dark in a neon lane-runner where your momentum is your speed, your life and your score all at once.

games.name: Scrapwall
games.description: Build a fort from scrap, then hold it — a co-op siege where the horde digs toward whatever wall you left weakest.

games.name: Tiny Tanks
games.description: Bank ricochet shots around the walls, steal the enemy flag, and race it home — a top-down capture-the-flag tank duel. Solo with bots or peer-to-peer with friends.

games.name: Grainfall
games.description: Rule a city-state one year at a time — split the grain, sow the fields, feed your people, and survive the harvests, rats and plagues that decide your reign.

games.name: Delvepack
games.description: Descend a monster-choked dungeon — clear each floor, grab an upgrade, dash to dodge, go deeper. Solo, or drop in a friend and revive each other.

games.name: Gloamrun
games.description: Descend the gloam together — a co-op dungeon crawl where you fight deeper floor by floor, revive each other, and see how far the dark lets you go.

games.name: Morsel
games.description: Eat the small ones, outrun the big ones — but catching anyone costs you the very mass you were winning with.

games.name: Driftlock
games.description: You never move a stone — you shift the row it stands on, and whatever slides into the rising Well is yours.

games.name: Windup
games.description: Program three moves, wind it up, and watch it all go wrong as the bots shove each other off the ripening cogs.

games.name: Bidstorm
games.description: Everyone holds the same thirteen cards — outbid your rivals for each prize, and never spend more than you had to.

games.name: Lumenlock
games.description: Flip mirrors to bend a beam through a prism, splitting white light into a rainbow, and lock every crystal in its own colour.

games.name: Nightwire
games.description: Hidden-role deduction where the clues are numbers: probe a seat to learn how many Ghosts sit in that window, and remember the Ghosts choose what they publish.

games.name: Orbital Skirmish
games.description: Thrust and slingshot around a lethal star that pulls ships, bullets and rocks alike, and be the last ship flying — solo against waves, or live with 2–4 friends.

games.name: Gravity Golf
games.description: Slingshot your ball through a field of planets and bend it around gravity into the hole.

games.name: Snake Royale
games.description: Classic snake in a shared arena — eat, grow and cut your rivals off; last snake slithering wins.

games.name: Rhythm Relay
games.description: Relay the beat down two lanes, tap in time to keep a shared combo alive, and take a lane each with a friend.

games.name: Hexbloom
games.description: Pick a colour to bloom your blob across the honeycomb and claim more tiles than your rivals.

games.name: Cipher Clash
games.description: Trace words on a shared letter grid and race to claim them before your rival does.
